**Probably not, but it's close.** I put VLTG's 2027 revenue at roughly C$3.9–4.2B, so C$4.2B is the top of the range and would need everything to go right. This rests on thin data and on the two child nodes' summaries (n2.r1, n3.r1). I didn't open the underlying documents myself.

- **Company disclosures (n2):**
  - Orders rose 11% year on year in H1 2026, led by utility and data-centre customers.
  - A fire halted the Halbrook plant for nine weeks in Q2 2026. Halbrook builds all of Voltaris's large power transformers. It restarted in August at full capacity.
  - About C$310M of delayed shipments are due between Q4 2026 and Q2 2027, on top of normal output. That recovery helps 2027 but isn't enough to guarantee the guidance.
  - n2 puts 2027 revenue at about C$3.9–4.2B, so the guidance is possible but needs everything to go right.
- **Industry data (n3):**
  - Industry transformer shipments fell 4% year on year in Q2 2026, the first decline in three years.
  - Voltaris shipments fell 9% in that quarter, the steepest decline among large makers. Tarnwell grew 4% and imports grew 11%.
  - On this basis n3 puts 2027 revenue well below C$4.2B. It rests on two quarters of shipment growth and one quarter of share data.

The two views differ mainly on how much of the Halbrook outage was a one-off. The company's own figures treat it as temporary and recoverable. The industry data shows share loss to Tarnwell and imports, which may not reverse.
